subject: Archaeology
title: Hadrian's Wall: Edge of Empire
description: A quick, practical guide to Hadrian's Wall: Edge of Empire.

hook.text: Rome built a 73-mile wall across northern England. It was not just a barrier — it was a customs checkpoint.

buildup.text: Emperor Hadrian ordered the wall in 122 CE. It had forts, milecastles, watchtowers, and a road running behind it.

discovery.text: At Vindolanda fort, archaeologists found wooden tablets with soldiers' letters — including birthday invitations.

twist.text: One letter begs for warm socks and underpants. Roman soldiers on the frontier were cold and miserable.

climax.text: The Vindolanda tablets are the oldest handwritten documents in Britain — 2,000-year-old personal mail.

punchline.text: Rome's frontier soldiers wanted the same thing modern soldiers do: warm socks.

quiz.question: What did the Vindolanda tablets from Hadrian's Wall reveal?
options: Battle plans for defending against northern invasions
Personal letters including birthday invitations and requests for warm clothes
Financial records showing the cost of building the wall
